On the tube λ₀+λ₁≥3/4, so the projective coordinates are valid on the entire set. Differentiating λ₁ in t gives (1+y+z)^−1 and the (λ₂,λ₃) Jacobian gives (1+y+z)^−3. The product is the claimed volume factor up to a fixed constant.

For an arbitrary nonempty collection, the radial profile is a supremum of nonnegative continuous affine-in-t cutoff functions with positive polar denominators. It is convex in t, lower semicontinuous jointly, finite by the tube bound, and integrates correctly even at a zero cutoff or an unattained radial endpoint. The empty union gives the identically zero density.

The radial cutoff satisfies kR_α(t)≤1/3 because kr/(1+kr)≤1/4 for every radius below a positive cutoff. The derivative of r(1+kr)^−4 is (1−3kr)/(1+kr)^5, so W_k is increasing convex on the whole permitted interval. Composition and angular integration preserve convexity.

Convexity and reflection make g(t)=f(t)+f(1−t) nonincreasing on [0,1/2]. The mass on the middle half is at most half the total. The cap H₂ or H₃ can occur only on a null set in the tube. The conditions H₀⇒t≤3/4 and H₁⇒t≥1/4 bound multiplicity as stated. Integrating gives 3/2 and 27/16−3/2=3/16.

overlap.comparison: For a convex ambient body it derives a density with convex inverse power for an affine projective marginal. An arbitrary strict trace union need not be convex, and the conclusion here is convexity of the density itself with a tube-specific multiplicity bound.
